To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency control of an autonomous island system can be improved with wind power penetration by using a combination of inertial and droop responses of the wind turbines.
the frequency control of island power systems can be improved with the participation of WTs, which is a very important issue, especially for systems with high wind power penetration.

the frequency control in islanded autonomous power systems with high wind penetration can be improved by using WTs with a droop characteristic, and that the droop characteristics of WTs can be designed to be similar to the droop characteristic of conventional synchronous machines, so that they can provide the same frequency support as conventional synchronous generators.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) The contribution of WTs in the frequency control of autonomous power systems with high penetration levels, (2) The investigation and comparison of different methods for WT frequency control participation, (3) The quantitative analysis of the expected benefits and limitations of each method, and (4) The appropriate selection of the parameters of each method.

the following: (1) the impact of wind power on the frequency response of autonomous power systems; (2) a comparative study of the different types of wind turbines; (3) the capability of the wind power system to participate in the frequency control; (4) the appropriate selection of wind turbines parameters for frequency control; and (5) the expected benefits and the potential drawbacks.

the following issues: 1) How to define the primary frequency response of the wind farm (WF) and its contribution to the system frequency control 2) How to define and select the appropriate parameters of the WT control system, in order to provide the maximum contribution to the frequency regulation of the system 3) How the different WT types can participate in the system frequency control, and which are the advantages and disadvantages of each type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ASIG WTs are capable of providing a significant amount of primary reserve and primary frequency control.
WTs are capable of contributing to the frequency control and offer reserve in island autonomous systems.
, in the case of the island system of Rhodes, the DFIG and PMSG WTs are able to offer a significant contribution in the frequency control of the power system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WTs can provide primary frequency control, but their contribution depends on the specific type of WT and the control method applied.
WTs can provide a significant contribution to the frequency regulation of noninterconnected islands.
the ASIG is the only type that can offer inertial response and primary reserve, the DFIG can only offer inertial response, and the PMSG can only offer primary reserve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WTs can offer a valuable contribution to the primary frequency control of non-interconnected island power systems.
WTs are able to provide a significant contribution to the frequency regulation of autonomous power systems.
WTs can contribute to the frequency control, but their participation in the frequency regulation is highly dependent on their characteristics.
